limitations: Source amplitude, receiver noise, threshold offset and AM depth are explicit hypotheses, not a qualified input circuit.
Two declared downstream noise allocations; stationary white-equivalent noise in 1 kHz–8 MHz.
Input AM at 1 MHz; cyclostationary additive-noise modulation omitted.
Source PM passes with unity gain; loaded sideband dispersion, stage power/startup and supply correlation unqualified.
Absolute static propagation delay omitted; no latency or input-circuit qualification.
input_noise_reference.source_peak_interpretation: Gain-equivalent ideal-ground parameter only; physical amplitude is physical_source_peak_v.

electrical.scope: Conservative declared port voltage/current/energy bounds; no physical parameter validation, clipping waveform, noise or matching-network qualification

transmitter.scope: Selected native 10-bit DAC and third-order reconstruction at the existing 20 MHz wideband cutoff. Same shared rail/reference/clock realization as RX, external observer with ideal framing and known DATA training. Broad power bands are not a spectral mask. A supplied driver-wake trajectory changes rail/reference/timing and available tail-current limit within the existing 28 mA reservation; otherwise warm constant bias. No signal-dependent RF-cycle current, physical DAC glitches, real FIFO/control lifecycle or external RF filtering. Output impedance/distortion and ENOB remain assigned requirements.

scope: 240 mA full-mode budget, full internal pulses, 500 pF/current package target, 1 V source, negative 0.025 ps/mV. Single-ended and 20% aligned-mismatch paired input. Driver starts warm or ramps from 0 to its already-budgeted 28 mA at nominal source start, in 20 ns or 1 us. Coupled rail/input/reference/delay and available tail-current limit are applied. Early waveform is compared with matched warm output without fitting away phase/amplitude. No physical bias-readiness, RF switch, preamble, TX mask, signal-dependent DAC/driver current or protocol turnaround qualification.
